newsitem.title: UK: ASDA's Norman slams lottery profits.
newsitem.headline: ASDA's Norman slams lottery profits.

text.p: Archie Norman, the exuberant head of British supermarket group ASDA who will stand for the ruling Conservatives at the next election, criticised the National Lottery on Thursday and vowed the new midweek lottery profits, generated by ASDA, would go directly to charity. "We do not believe in giving money away through some anonymous committee," Norman said in a statement. "People want to see more of their lottery money going to charity and to the kind of causes they support," he added.
The Midweek Lottery launches shortly and will be run by Camelot Group Plc, which already operates the weekly lottery which takes place on Saturday.
Norman said ASDA's profits from the sale of midweek lottery tickets could amount to some 250,000 pounds ($405,100) in the first year.

"If other major lottery ticket retailers adopted our profit-free stance, extra millions of pounds would go straight to good causes," Norman said. Camelot gives a proportion of its profits to "Good Causes," which are chosen by several government-appointed bodies.
But the lottery and Camelot, which won the contract to operate it in 1994 from the Conservative government, have both come under fierce criticism for making huge profits.

The Opposition Labour party, well ahead of the Conservatives in polls with a general election due by May, has said it would prefer the operator to be non-profit making and that it would look at ways to curb profits while Camelot's licence runs.

Norman, who will stand for the safe seat of Tunbridge Wells in Kent, has already riled party colleagues with predictions that it will be tough for the Conservatives to win the election and says that a member of parliament's job could be part-time. The ASDA Foundation is run by company employees and its three focus areas for the current year are victims of crime, women's health and better education for children.
